newsitem.title: UK: FASHANU USED WIFE'S ACCOUNT TO RECEIVE MONEY - COURT.
newsitem.headline: FASHANU USED WIFE'S ACCOUNT TO RECEIVE MONEY - COURT.

text.p: The wife of former England and Wimbledon striker John Fashanu told his match-rigging trial on Friday that her husband used her bank accounts to receive loan money.
Melissa Kassa Mapsi, the daughter of a former vice prime minister of Gabon, was charged with her husband and the other three defendants but the accusations against her were later dropped.
She told the court in the southern English town of Winchester that Fashanu had asked her about using her bank account in Britain and France some time in 1991.
"He said this money was loan money. He wanted to keep it separate from his ordinary money which was income money so he would not have to pay tax on the loan money," she said.
"I remember John asking me if I had an account overseas. When I said yes, he said it's even better to put the loan money into an overseas account so it is clear."

Fashanu, who has declined to testify in the high-profile trial, is accused of conspiring to give and accept money from a Far Eastern betting syndicate as inducements to influence the outcome of soccer matches.

The player-turned-television presenter has denied the charges along with his co-defendants , Zimbabwean-born former Liverpool goalkeeper Bruce Grobbelaar, Dutch keeper Hans Segers and Malaysian businessman Heng Suan Lim.
Mapsi, whose native language is French, described how she met Fashanu in London in 1990, and said they married in a Moslem ceremony in January 1995. Their son was born the following November.
She was arrested in March 1995 when she was two months pregnant. Because of language difficulties, she did not understand what police were talking about when they arrived at her home at dawn.

"I was on bail twice after the arrest and it was I think in October when we were getting ready to go back for a court appearance and they told my solicitor on the phone that the charge against me had been dropped," she said.
When questioned about large deposits in her accounts from Indonesia, Mapsi denied she had any contacts with people there. The money was not hers, she added.
Fashanu, who reached the peak of his fame as a soccer player with Wimbledon in the late 1980s, juggled his obligations to the club with a successful career as a media personality.
He presented a television game show and acts as a special representative for the United Nations Children Fund (UNICEF) to Africa.

Abandoned by his Nigerian father, he and his footballing brother Justin were brought up by foster parents in England. He played twice for England in 1989 and 324 times for Wimbledon, scoring 129 times.
A knee injury forced him to retire in 1994, shortly after his move to Midlands side Aston Villa.
